Task: Develop a complete lesson plan for teaching probability to high-school students.

Lesson Plan: Introduction to Probability  
Grade Level: 9–10 (adaptable 8–12)  
Duration: One 55-minute class period (with options for extension/homework)  
Standards Alignment (sample)  
• CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS.MD.A.1–2 (calculating & interpreting probabilities)  
• NGSS Science Practice 4 (analyzing & interpreting data)  
• ISTE 4a (using technology to analyze data)

--------------------------------------------------
1. Learning Objectives  
By the end of the lesson students will be able to …  
1. Define probability and distinguish between theoretical & experimental probability.  
2. Calculate simple probabilities of single events (P(A) = favorable outcomes / total outcomes).  
3. Experimentally estimate probabilities with manipulatives and compare to theoretical values.  
4. Describe events as certain, likely, unlikely, impossible, or equally likely.  
5. Translate real-world contexts (weather, sports, games) into probability statements.

--------------------------------------------------
2. Materials & Technology  
• One 6-sided die per pair (OR coin, spinner, or digital dice app)  
• Bag with 20 colored beads (8 red, 6 blue, 4 green, 2 yellow) per group  
• Student handout (definitions, guided notes, practice problems)  
• Projector/interactive board + short slide deck  
• Optional: Desmos “Marble Slides: Probability” or GeoGebra probability simulation  
• Exit ticket slips / Google Form  
• Large “likelihood line” poster (0 to 1 continuum)

--------------------------------------------------
3. Lesson Sequence (55 min)

0:00–0:05  Hook / Activate Prior Knowledge  
• Display weather forecast screenshot: “40 % chance of rain.”  
• Ask: “What does 40 % mean? Will it rain?” Quick think-pair-share → connect to probability.

0:05–0:12  Concept Introduction  
• Define probability (P(A) = number of favorable outcomes ÷ total outcomes).  
• Differentiate theoretical vs. experimental with simple coin‐flip example.  
• Place terms on the Likelihood Line: impossible (0), unlikely (<0.5), equally likely (0.5), likely (>0.5), certain (1).

0:12–0:20  Guided Practice #1 – Dice Demo (Whole Class)  
• Ask: “What is the theoretical probability of rolling a 4?” Write 1/6 = 0.167 ≈ 17 %.  
• Roll a die 12 times, tally on board, compute experimental proportion together. Discuss why results differ from theory and how sample size matters (Law of Large Numbers lite).

0:20–0:30  Hands-On Group Activity – Bead Bag Investigation  
• Groups of 3-4. Predict theoretical probabilities from bag counts (e.g., P(red)=8/20=0.4).  
• Each student draws, records, and replaces 25 beads (100 trials per group).  
• Groups compile results, calculate experimental probabilities, and create bar chart (manual or digital).  
• Prompt guiding questions on handout.

0:30–0:35  Debrief / Connections  
• Each group posts/share quick comparison chart.  
• Discuss variation, reasons, and what would happen with 1,000+ trials (connect to sampling).

0:35–0:45  Guided Practice #2 – Real-World Scenarios (Think-Pair-Share)  
Display three scenarios; students compute & discuss:  
A. Basketball player makes 7 of 10 free throws; estimate probability of next free throw.  
B. Bag has 5 cherry, 3 lemon, 2 grape candies. P(grape)? P(not cherry)?  
C. Card deck: probability of drawing a heart or an ace?  
Teacher circulates, then reviews answers with class.

0:45–0:50  Independent Practice / Formative Check  
Handout 4 skill questions + 1 challenge:  
1. P(rolling an even number)? 2. P(drawing red bead)? 3. Weather report with 0.2 rain, 0.3 cloudy, 0.5 sunny – verify probabilities. 4. Write event on likelihood line. Challenge: “What’s the minimum number of coin flips to be at least 95 % sure of getting at least one head?” (binomial; extension)

0:50–0:53  Exit Ticket (Assessment)  
• Define theoretical vs. experimental probability in one sentence each.  
• Compute P(blue) from bead bag example.  
Collect or use Google Form for instant feedback.

0:53–0:55  Reflection / Preview Next Lesson  
• Ask: “How would probability change if events are combined (like two dice)?”  
• Explain that tomorrow they’ll study compound probability & tree diagrams.

--------------------------------------------------
4. Differentiation & UDL

Readiness  
• Pre-teach vocabulary with picture glossary.  
• Provide calculator & fractional/decimal equivalence chart.

Learning Profiles  
• Auditory (discussion), visual (charts, likelihood line), kinesthetic (bead draws).  
• ELL: sentence frames (“The probability of ___ is ___ because ___.”).

Enrichment  
• Ask advanced students to derive formula for NOT A (complement), or explore conditional probability in “Monty Hall” simulation.

--------------------------------------------------
5. Assessment Plan  
• Formative: teacher observation during activities, guided questions, exit ticket.  
• Summative (next class/quiz): problems mixing theoretical, experimental, and real-world interpretations.

--------------------------------------------------
6. Reflection (Teacher Notes – after lesson)  
• Which misconception appeared? (e.g., “law of averages” expectation)  
• Did hands-on activity improve conceptual grasp?  
• Adjust bead ratios or number of trials next time? Etc.

--------------------------------------------------
7. Homework / Extension (Optional)  
Option 1: Virtual coin-flip simulation for 200 trials; screenshot results & compare to 50-trial class data.  
Option 2: “Find three real news headlines that quote a probability or percentage; explain event and its probability interpretation.”
